findings: Buddy raises his chin toward the glowing jellyfish while Neet directs a skeptical sideways look toward him; Heather stands immediately beside the dogs. This depicts the shared primary/shortened-story quiet beat.

Buddy has a continuous full moderately elongated trunk, visible neck and substantial separated legs with four floor-supported paws; Neet has a full narrow trunk, fine legs, broad triangular ears and visible tiny nub. Far-side overlap beside Heather remains intelligible.

Bodies use broad smooth color shapes rather than curls or engraved fur; Buddy furnishings remain concentrated at muzzle, brows, ears and modest distal edges. No material shag-volume or short-coat drift observed.

Tank glass, dry reflective visitor floor, planted shadows and background scale make the spatial arrangement coherent. Blue lighting does not erase tan/charcoal identities. Human likeness remains provisional.
Neet crouches behind Buddy as the shark passes overhead; Buddy turns back without moving away, supporting the sheltering action and contrast between alarm and reassurance.

Neet has connected folded hindquarters and distinct planted forepaws; the near and far rear paw shapes remain attached to the folded pose. Buddy has four separate supported limbs, uninterrupted trunk and neck, real clearance and a slender dark tail. Their overlap does not merge limb ownership.

Both torso surfaces are smooth painted planes, with no curled engraving or raised shag contour. Buddy pale brows/moustache and hanging ear furnishings remain localized; Neet triangular ears and tiny rump nub remain readable.
Converging tunnel arches, shark beyond glass and feet on one dry floor establish perspective. Expressions carry the comedy without extra lettering or distracting artifacts.
